statements.proposition: After this change, Shuffle, Bzip2Filter and Lz4Filter (structs with no inner constructor) still accept positional arguments via Julia's automatic constructors.
statements.label: TRUE
statements.note: Julia not installed, so not run. By language semantics an added outer keyword constructor does not suppress the default positional constructor of a struct without an inner constructor. The PR's own tests exercise Shuffle(UInt32(8)), Bzip2Filter(5), Lz4Filter(12345). Deflate and ZstdFilter keep an explicit positional inner constructor.
evidence: gh api pulls/682/files patch of src/Filters.jl: struct Shuffle has no inner constructor; only Shuffle(; element_size=0) outer added
patch of JLD2Bzip2.jl and JLD2Lz4.jl: structs keep only field declarations; outer keyword constructors replace zero-arg ones
patch of test/compression.jl adds @test Bzip2Filter(5).blocksize100k == 5, Lz4Filter(12345).blocksize == 12345, Shuffle(UInt32(8)).element_size == 8

statements.proposition: This change maintains full backward compatibility of the filter APIs (no behaviour change for existing usage).
statements.label: FALSE
statements.note: ZstdFilter behaviour changed: old constructor clamped level to [1, maxCLevel]; new one removes the lower clamp (min only), so ZstdFilter(0) or negative levels now store those values instead of 1. The field type changed from Cuint to Int32 and client_values now uses level % UInt32. The PR's CHANGELOG itself says 'Allow negative compression levels for the ZstdFilter'. Not run (no Julia), but the behaviour difference is read directly from the diff.
evidence: patch of src/Filters.jl: removed 'new(clamp(level, 1, ZSTD_maxCLevel()))', added 'new(min(level % Int32, ZSTD_maxCLevel()))'; field level::Cuint -> level::Int32
patch of CHANGELOG.md: 'Allow negative compression levels for the ZstdFilter'
